articles.title: Preventing a Health Service Continuity Crisis in Syria - Donor Briefing Note - Evidence period: 2025 and 2026 Impact of Underfunding of Health Sector Syria June 2026
articles.description: Country: Syrian Arab Republic Sources: Health Cluster, World Health Organization Please refer to the attached file. Syria is at a narrow recovery window, but health-service underfunding is cutting off care just as needs, returns, disease risks, and pressure on damaged public systems are rising. Immediate bridge funding and flexible multi-year support are needed to prevent avoidable deaths, protect frontline capacity, and keep recovery from reversing into renewed humanitarian dependence. Underfunding in 2026 is already translating into reduced operational capacity and full-service suspensions across the Syria health response. The most urgent donor concern is timing: 90 underfunded sector projects’ activities ended between January – June 2026. Immediate bridge funding, flexible reprogramming, and targeted prioritization are needed to prevent a sequence of closures and service cuts.

articles.title: ‘I’ve sat at the very precipice of life’: Clarke Carlisle on gambling, depression – and survival
articles.description: The former professional footballer has struggled with his mental health for most of his life. But it took five suicide attempts for him to admit how badly he wanted to end it. He talks about how he turned the corner – and his hopes for his new post with the charity Mind ‘How are you?” I ask Clarke Carlisle. Usually when you meet people it’s a nicety. Not with Carlisle. He smiles ecstatically. “I’m incredibly well, thank you. Yeah, really, really good,” says the former footballer and incoming chair of the mental health charity Mind. “I have been consistently well – not just stable, but well – for three or four years now.” Few people understand what it is to be mentally unwell quite like Carlisle does. And few understand what recovery means like he does. “It doesn’t happen by accident. Once you get stable that’s not the end of the journey. And that seems to be the MO of our society these days. You do something, you go into hospital and they patch you up, then send you on your way. And that’s the same with mental health. You might get some pills, have a counselling session, you might have a hug and a chat with someone, and they think that’s the end of the journey. And it’s not.” Continue reading...

articles.title: South Sudan: Rapid Ebola Virus Disease Knowledge Assessment in High-Risk Areas, July 2026
articles.description: Countries: South Sudan, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda Source: REACH Initiative Please refer to the attached file. Key Messages • Despite widespread awareness of EVD, findings indicate some respondents do not believe outbreaks are occurring in neighbouring countries, as well as relatively low levels of risk perception, especially in Juba. • Health workers and the radio seemed to be the most widely used and trusted sources of health information, but qualitative information suggests more remote communities may not have access to either. • Respondents seemed able to recall some common symptoms of EVD, but both survey findings and qualitative data indicate a widespread desire for additional information.
